intro.title: What Mirasim is
intro.sub: One Agent IDE — the agent that writes your code and the simulated user that tests it, in the same workbench.
intro.body: In the usual workflow you write code in one tool, then open the page yourself to check it. Mirasim connects those two ends: coding agents work in parallel inside the workbench, and when a build is ready, simulated users actually use your product in a real browser or a real mobile emulator and bring the first-hand feedback back. These are the core capabilities listed on the official site:

cards.p: Several projects side by side, each with its own sessions, agents and model configuration — nothing bleeds across.
Run many agent sessions at once, with a VS Code-like editor for quick edits. Works from mobile too.

cards.h: Terminal and GUI, one keystroke apart
cards.p: The same workflow either way: keyboard-driven in the TUI, point-and-browse in the GUI.

cards.h: Automation that reads structure, not screenshots
cards.p: The agent reads pages as text structure — roughly 184 B against 60 KB for a screenshot, about 330× less data — driving real Chrome with a real user profile.
Mac apps, the iOS Simulator and the Android emulator answer the same way, so mobile products get tested by simulated users too.

cards.h: A single tool entry saves context
cards.p: The official figure is about 1k tokens of tool overhead per turn, against roughly 53k for thirty tool schemas — the context stays with the work.

intro.callout: Mirasim is in Alpha; the official wording is "expect rough edges". Once installed, the app keeps itself up to date.

models.title: Models you can use for free
models.sub: The invite code costs nothing, and Mirasim itself runs on the model accounts you already have.
models.p1: The official wording is "a code costs nothing and runs on your own model accounts": using Mirasim with an invite code is free. Bring the Claude Code or Codex subscription you already pay for, or an API key, and you get those agents plus Mirasim's own agent, the six-pane workbench, MCP servers and plugins — Mirasim charges nothing on top.
models.p2: If you do buy credits, the models the platform can call directly cover most of the field:
models.callout1: No silent model swaps: the official pricing page states "you get the model you picked". Any turn that fell back is marked as such in the record, and there is a fingerprint method published so you can check for yourself.
models.callout2: Two exceptions: computer use and simulated users spend cloud quota, so they need a paid plan or an API key of your own. Everything else works on a free account.

invite.title: Invite rewards: a free month of Pro
invite.sub: Invite people who genuinely use Mirasim and the team covers a full month of a paid plan for you.
invite.body: The rule that matters: sign-ups alone do not count. The people you invite have to actually use Mirasim — sign in, open sessions, do real work — and the team checks. Once you are in, your own invite code lives under Settings → Account; if you have run out, the official Discord hands out more.
invite.callout: You can start today: activate your account with this wiki's code {code} (copy it at the top), then share the code you get. Five real users is a free month of Pro — $89 the team pays instead of you.

pricing.title: Paid plans at a glance
pricing.sub: Credits pay for calls to the official cloud models, including computer use and simulated users. Run out and you can switch back to your own account and keep working.
pricing.callout: The official comparison: the same usage runs about $40–$400 a month elsewhere (a Claude Code and a Codex subscription each). Per-model credit rates are published. Full details at mirasim.ai/pricing.

items.q: How do I actually get the free month of Pro?
items.a: Invite 5 builders who really use Mirasim. Sign-ups alone explicitly do not count — they have to sign in, open sessions and do real work, and the team verifies before granting the month. The same scheme gives one month of Basic for 3 people and one month of Max for 10.

items.q: How do I check the download has not been tampered with?
items.a: Every file's SHA-256 is listed in the download table (click to copy), or fetch the official SHA256SUMS and run shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing. All links point at the official CDN (cdn-assets.mirasim.ai); this wiki hosts no packages of its own.
